calibration_notes.summary: All 48 accepted items were re-rated by an independent rubric rater (answer-free). Author labels: 12 easy / 24 medium / 12 hard. Calibrated: 14 / 25 / 9. Changes: 5 hard to medium, 3 medium to easy, 2 medium to hard, 1 easy to medium. The rater also solved every item, and all 48 answers match the keys. Accepted records are unchanged; calibrated labels are in calibration/act_math.json and drive targeting and the import export difficulty. From batch 6 on, the blind solver applies the same rubric (v2), and a hard-labelled item rated easy goes to REVISE.
Calibration now uses tools/calibrate.py: the median of every independent rating (per-batch blind solver plus three rater files). At 208 items: 52 easy / 120 medium / 36 hard.

calibration_notes.finding: After 177 accepted verbal items (English 55, Reading 55, SAT 67), the first blind rater has rated none hard; author labels had 18 hard. Calibrated verbal mix is about 55% easy / 45% medium / 0% hard, far from the 25/50/25 target. SAT batch 7 was a deliberate hard-item experiment (dissolved vs resolved, base rates, subordinate-clause boundaries, only-when interaction data); both raters put every item at 45-72% est. correct (medium/easy).
calibration_notes.interpretation: Partly real (short passages of about 250-400 words versus about 700-900 on real ACT Reading [likely]; few dense or archaic texts) and partly a rater ceiling (AI raters rarely estimate below 45% correct for any verbal item that has a single defensible key). Without human response data this cannot be separated.
actions: Next verbal batches: longer, denser ACT Reading passages, literary and older-style prose, more paired-text synthesis, and fewer items whose distractors are plainly out of scope.
Hard labels on verbal items are now assigned only to items with a specific trap that the author expects to catch most students; the hard gate keeps them honest.
At each 100-item verbal audit, add a second whole-bank rater so calibration is a median rather than one opinion.

calibration_notes.finding: A whole-bank AI rater re-rated all 103 SAT items: 31 easy / 63 medium / 9 hard, with no flawed items. Under the median rule (two ratings, so the lower middle value is used), the calibrated mix is 47 easy / 55 medium / 1 hard.

contested_items.issue: Restrictive vs nonrestrictive title ('Her book Silent Spring,'). The key (A, restrictive) follows the passage's cue that Carson wrote several books; 2 of 3 AI solvers agreed and the whole-bank rater chose B. Keep it, but flag it for human review before publication.

calibration_notes.note: The lower-middle median rule is deliberately conservative: an item is calibrated hard only when every rating so far agrees.

calibration_notes.finding: The whole-bank AI rater gave 109 English items 65 easy / 40 medium / 4 hard and found no flawed items. The hard items were faulty comparisons (x2), a restrictive appositive, and whoever-after-a-preposition. All nine essay-level 'did the essay meet this goal' items rated easy (78-82%). Too many rhetoric items have one obviously relevant choice and three throwaways.
actions: Rhetorical-skills items: make every distractor relevant to the passage and wrong for a specific reason (wrong placement, wrong scope, a near-miss on the stated goal), not off-topic filler.
Use essay-goal items sparingly, and make both 'No' choices plausible.
Favor conventions that are rarely taught explicitly (restrictive appositives, faulty comparisons, pronoun case after prepositions, subjunctive), which the raters actually find hard.

calibration_notes.finding: A fourth whole-bank AI rater (calibration/act_math_rater_2026-10-26d.json) rated 302 live items 46 easy / 218 medium / 38 hard and found no flawed items or key disagreements. Calibrated as the median across all raters: 24% easy / 63% medium / 13% hard. The only standing rater mismatch is the known slip on CLD-ACT-M-000130 (key A confirmed earlier).
calibration_notes.assessment: The math hard share (13%) is still below the 25% target. Items written as hard after batch 21 are usually rated medium; the hard ones that land need a construction or insight (tangent lines, face-area products, conditional reversal, period-doubling).
actions: Keep 3-4 hard attempts per math batch built on insight rather than computation.
Accept that AI raters rarely put more than about 15-20% of competent items under 40%; real student data would be needed to settle the true share.

human_review_status: none of the accepted items has had human editorial review
